title: usages
summary: Finds usage sites of a symbol in one of four scopes (this bound symbol, project, group, everywhere), with a choice of report width
intro: Read this when you want every place a symbol is used: usages (also behind Find Usages in the IDE) lists the grouped usage sites. --scope symbol (the default) answers the declaration a position (--in/--line/--col) or a qualified name is bound to; project, group and everywhere widen it to every object of that name in the project, the project group or every index.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint usages --name <X> | --in <file> --line <L> [--col <C>] [--scope symbol|project|group|everywhere] [--group <x.groupproj>] [--width narrow|wide|very-wide] [--db <path>] [--depth N] [--format json|--json] [--limit N] [--rw] [--in <file> [--no-create]] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>]
help: drag-lint usages             --name <X> | --in <file> --line <L> [--col <C>] [--scope symbol|project|group|everywhere] [--group <x.groupproj>] [--width narrow|wide|very-wide] [--db <path>] [--depth N] [--format json|--json] [--limit N] [--rw] [--in <file> [--no-create]] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>]
grouped usage report; backs the IDE Symbol Search dialog's Usages view.

--scope (1.52): symbol (default) = the declaration --in/--line/--col or a qualified --name is BOUND to, in this project; project = every object of the name in this project (symbol and project skip a library-*.sqlite --db unless every --db is one); group = the name in every project of --group <x.groupproj>; everywhere = the name in every index the manifest knows. A bare --name with no position binds nothing and is answered as scope project (the JSON says scope, scope_note, databases).
--limit N keeps the first N rows of each JSON group (declarations included) and adds
"limit" and "totals" (the full counts); without it nothing is capped.

--rw: the users of a member split into readers and writers, one block per declaration: a property with its backing field and accessor methods, a field with its properties, a getter (reads) or setter (writes). Rows name the route (property, field, getter, setter, direct).

With no --db, --in <file> finds the unit's project and its database. No DB: prints the index command, exits 2. Two projects list it: names both, exits 2. No project: a library unit on an assumed platform, unless it uses units the library lacks (names them, exits 2). With neither --db nor --in the verb exits 2.

steps: Put the caret on the symbol in the editor

questions.ask: How do I get a wider or JSON report?
Where is exactly the symbol at this position used, not its namesakes?
Where is this name used in every project of the group, or in every index?
